HabiroCohomologyFoundations.summary: Nothing specific to q-Hodge or Habiro cohomology exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Neither library has λ-rings, δ-rings or prisms, q-derivatives or q-de Rham complexes, animated rings, derived de Rham cohomology, décalage, q-Witt or de Rham–Witt complexes, Habiro-complete modules, or spectra. So HQ.2–HQ.6 and HQ.8 are unbuilt, HQ.1 is partly built only because its q-integer identities already exist, and HQ.7 is acceptance testing. What the libraries already have is generic support, all in Mathlib. The q-integer identities that HQ.1 calls prototype lemmas are there as geometric sums ([n]_q(q−1) = q^n − 1, Φ_p = [p]_q, Φ_p(1) = p). Mathlib also has p-typical Witt vectors with F, V and a ghost map (bijective only when p is invertible), Kähler differentials, underived filtrations, Tor, regular sequences, smooth and étale algebras, condensed and solid modules, and Fontaine's θ with B_dR⁺. HQ.1's local q-crystalline input duplicates PrismaticCohomology PR.6, HQ.2's derived de Rham/filtered/Lη/animation inputs duplicate DD.1–DD.2, AI.1 and EDS E5:animation, and HQ.5-trace restates RefinedTraceMethods RT.4:q-Hodge.

targets.target: q-integers [n]_q = ∑_{i<n} q^i with their interface identities: [n]_q·(q−1) = q^n − 1, the value at q = 1, and [p]_q = Φ_p(q), the generator of the q-prism ideal
targets.note: There is no separate name for [n]_q, but it is the geometric sum ∑_{i<n} X^i and these are its identities: `geom_sum_mul` holds in every ring, `Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime` identifies Φ_p with ∑_{i<p} X^i for p prime, `Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_prime` gives [p]_1 = Φ_p(1) = p (for general n, [n]_1 = n is `Polynomial.eval_geom_sum` followed by simp), and `cyclotomic_prime_pow_eq_geom_sum` gives [p]_{q^{p^n}} = Φ_{p^{n+1}}. The 'prototype q-integer lemmas' therefore need no new mathematics. Mathlib's Pochhammer file still lists q-factorials, q-binomials and q-Pochhammer symbols as TODO.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles.summary: No layer is built: neither library has nearby or vanishing cycles, étale direct images or base change, constructible or lisse sheaves, perverse sheaves, étale fundamental groups of schemes, blow-ups, Veronese embeddings, Bertini, Lefschetz pencils, p-adic Lie groups, tame characters, monodromy filtrations, semistable curves or invariant-cycle theorems. Mathlib supplies the surrounding infrastructure: étale and pro-étale sites, geometric points of the étale site (a conservative family), sheaf cohomology and pro-étale Hⁱ(X, ℤ_ℓ), t-structures, Galois categories, inertia subgroups and the cyclotomic character, and Zariski's lemma for points over finite extensions. Tau Ceti adds generic and special fibres over a DVR, numerical types of special fibres, function-field ramification groups, and generation of Sp by root subgroups. The linear algebra LPV asks to construct is largely in Mathlib already. Transvections come with their fixed spaces (the common fixed space of the local transvections is E^⊥), forms descend to quotients by their kernel with ker(B|_W) = W ∩ W^⊥, quadratic-form nondegeneracy follows Elman–Karpenko–Merkurjev in every characteristic (so the characteristic-2 polar-form distinction is already built), and nilpotent exponentials exist. Still missing are the unipotent logarithm and the monodromy filtration. LPV.0–2 are restated in WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.3, LPV.3–5 in R34.4, and LPV.4's radical quotient in DWP.3.

WeightsInEtaleCohomology.summary: WeightsInEtaleCohomology is an import interface for DeligneWeightsAndPurity and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles, and none of what it imports exists: neither library has Weil numbers or weights, Tate twists of étale sheaves, Tate modules, the Rosati involution, Weil I or II, hard Lefschetz, Kuga–Sato realisations or the Ramanujan–Deligne bound. The closest library content is Tau Ceti's elliptic-curve work towards the Hasse bound: deg(1 − π_q) = #E(F_q), a_q = q + 1 − #E(F_q), and the t² ≤ 4q endgame, the last still conditional on ℓ-torsion Frobenius matrices that need the unbuilt Weil pairing. Mathlib adds the house of an algebraic number and Kronecker's theorem (all conjugates of absolute value 1 gives a root of unity). R34.3 and R34.4 only import LPV.0–2/LPV.7 and LPV.3–5 and are process. R34.1, R34.2, R34.5 and R34.6 restate DWP.0, DWP.1, DWP.2–9 and DWP.10 respectively; R34.2 also restates WC.5's curve bound.

WeilConjectures.summary: Neither library has the zeta function of a variety over a finite field, étale cohomology with Frobenius, the trace formula, Poincaré duality, purity, Betti comparison, surface intersection theory or crystalline cohomology, so the cohomological spine of WC.1–WC.6 is unbuilt; WC.7 (worked examples and assembly) is process, and WC.0 is half bookkeeping (mapping a private repository onto owners) and half mathematics that neither library has (finiteness of X(F_{q^r}) for a separated finite-type scheme, and the canonical translations between point sets over isomorphic fields). What exists is the elementary shell. Mathlib has degree-n extensions of finite fields unique up to isomorphism with a cyclic Galois group generated by Frobenius, Möbius inversion, and irreducible polynomials dividing X^{q^n} − X exactly when their degree divides n. It also has Gauss's lemma, formal exp/log, the reversed characteristic polynomial det(1 − TM) with charpoly(A⁻¹) expressed through it, Newton's identities, and the point count |ℙ(k^{n+1})| = ∑ q^i. Tau Ceti adds finitely many places of bounded degree in a function field over a finite field, finiteness of the class group, genus and Riemann–Roch for curves, even dimension of real symplectic spaces, and for elliptic curves deg(1 − π_q) = #E(F_q) with a Hasse endgame still conditional on the Weil pairing. Genuinely missing even at the elementary level: finiteness of X(F_{q^r}) for schemes, the relation N_r = ∑ m·a_m, Fatou's lemma, the q^d-similitude reciprocity, the power-sum converse lemma, and the unconditional Hasse bound. WC.5:surface-alternative restates SF.5, WC.2's determinant step restates EDC.8, and WC.5 restates DWP.1/R34.2.

FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums.summary: Mathlib already contains most of FF.0 and FF.1, which the roadmap describes as things to build. For FF.0 it has classification and cardinality of finite fields, Frobenius generating the cyclic Galois group, subfields by divisibility (with Tau Ceti's uniqueness of the subfield of each order), explicit trace and norm formulas with surjectivity, and the normal basis theorem. For FF.1 it has additive and multiplicative characters with zero extension and the primitive trace character, the row orthogonality relations (with Tau Ceti supplying the column relation for every finite commutative group valued in a domain with enough roots of unity, hence for F_q^×), and Gauss and Jacobi sums with g(χ)g(χ⁻¹) = q, J = gg/g, J·J(χ⁻¹,φ⁻¹) = q and g^n = χ(−1)q∏J. Genuinely missing there: tensor decompositions, certified computable presentations and the Hasse–Davenport relations. FF.2 is unbuilt (no Weil or Deligne bounds, Kloosterman sums or trace functions). FF.3 has only ingredients: unique factorisation, the X^{q^n} − X irreducibility criterion, Tau Ceti's factor-degree certificates, and Hensel for simple roots over ℤ_p; there are no factoring or point-counting algorithms. FF.4 has only truncated Witt vectors (implicit Galois rings), linear codes with generator matrices, and finite abelian Fourier analysis; linearised and permutation polynomials, recurring-sequence correlation, evaluation/BCH/AG codes and finite upper half-planes are absent. FF.5 is a handoff. FF.1's Gauss/Jacobi sums restate CA.1, FF.3's certified factorisation restates CN.1, and FF.4's additive polynomials restate DM.0.

targets.target: Classification and cardinality of finite fields (reused)
targets.note: Every finite field has prime-power order; GaloisField p n has p^n elements; finite fields of equal cardinality are isomorphic, as fields and as algebras over a common base.

targets.target: Certified presentations F_q ≅ F_p[X]/(f) with checked irreducible f and field isomorphisms carrying explicit inverse maps
targets.note: The mathematics is in Mathlib: AdjoinRoot of an irreducible polynomial is a field, finite extensions have primitive elements, fields of equal cardinality are isomorphic, and an irreducible polynomial divides X^{q^n} − X exactly when its degree divides n (the basis of an irreducibility test). Missing: computable, certified presentations with irreducibility certificates and explicitly computed inverse isomorphisms; the library isomorphisms are noncomputable.

targets.target: Absolute and relative Frobenius with explicit exponents, generating the cyclic Galois group
targets.note: The p-power Frobenius of any characteristic-p ring, the relative q-power Frobenius as an algebra automorphism of an extension of F_q, its order [L:K], and generation of Gal(L/K) by it.

targets.target: Subfields: F_{p^m} embeds in F_{p^n} iff m ∣ n, with [K:F] embeddings, and uniqueness of the subfield of each admissible order
targets.note: Mathlib gives the divisibility criterion and the count of embeddings. Tau Ceti proves that in a separably closed field of characteristic p the subfield with p^n elements is exactly the fixed field of the p^n-power Frobenius, and that this fixed field has p^n elements.

targets.target: Trace and norm with explicit targets: Tr(x) = ∑ x^{q^i}, N(x) = x^{(q^n−1)/(q−1)}, surjectivity and nondegeneracy
targets.note: Explicit Frobenius-orbit formulas for trace and norm, surjectivity of the norm and (for separable extensions, which covers finite fields) of the trace, and nondegeneracy of the trace form to the prime field.

targets.target: Normal bases
targets.note: The normal basis theorem is proved for every finite Galois extension, and extensions of finite fields are Galois by an instance in Mathlib/FieldTheory/Finite/GaloisField.lean.

targets.target: Tensor decompositions F_{q^m} ⊗_{F_q} F_{q^n} ≅ F_{q^{lcm(m,n)}}^{gcd(m,n)}
targets.note: Not stated in either library. Mathlib only has the general theory of totally split algebras, including that finite étale algebras over a separably closed field split.

targets.target: Additive characters of F_q, including the canonical primitive character through the trace
targets.note: AddChar on any additive group, primitivity, and a primitive additive character of a finite field built as a primitive character of ZMod p composed with the trace (target of different characteristic).

targets.target: Multiplicative characters extended by zero, with the trivial-character case separated
targets.note: MulChar sends every non-unit to 0 by definition, so zero values are extended uniformly. The quadratic character is a special case. The trivial-character Gauss and Jacobi sums have their own lemmas.

targets.target: Orthogonality relations for additive and multiplicative characters
targets.note: Mathlib has the row relations: ∑_x ψ(x) = #A·[ψ = 0] for an additive character and ∑_x χ(x) = 0 for a nontrivial multiplicative character (the general form being `sum_hom_units_eq_zero` in Mathlib/RingTheory/IntegralDomain.lean:186), and the column relation only in specialisations (Dirichlet characters modulo n; complex-valued additive characters of a finite abelian group). Tau Ceti proves the column relation in the generality this layer needs: for any finite commutative group G and any domain M with enough roots of unity, ∑_{χ : G →* Mˣ} χ(g) is Nat.card G at g = 1 and 0 otherwise, which covers F_q^× for an arbitrary prime power q.

targets.target: Gauss sums with the norm identity g(χ,ψ)·g(χ⁻¹,ψ⁻¹) = q and g(χ,ψ)² = χ(−1)·q for quadratic χ
targets.note: Stated for a nontrivial χ and a primitive ψ on a finite field, with values in any integral domain. For complex-valued characters this gives |g|² = q once χ⁻¹ and ψ⁻¹ are identified with complex conjugates, a step not stated separately.

targets.target: Jacobi sums and their product identities: J(χ,φ) = g(χ)g(φ)/g(χφ), J(χ,φ)·J(χ⁻¹,φ⁻¹) = q, and g(χ)^n = χ(−1)·q·∏ J(χ,χ^i)
targets.note: All three identities are proved with their nontriviality hypotheses.

targets.target: The Hasse–Davenport lifting relation (Gauss sums of χ∘N_{F_{q^n}/F_q}) and the Hasse–Davenport product formula, if 'norm/product identities' includes them
targets.note: Neither library has the Hasse–Davenport lifting relation or product formula (no occurrence of Hasse–Davenport in either tree), nor Stickelberger's theorem on the p-adic valuation of Gauss sums. The names do occur elsewhere and are unrelated: Tau Ceti's TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean proves Stickelberger's congruence disc ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4 for a number field, and Mathlib's Davenport is Cauchy–Davenport in additive combinatorics.

Only the first half of WC.0 is bookkeeping. It also requires finiteness of X(F_{q^r}) for a separated finite-type k-scheme as a proved theorem and the canonical translations between point sets over isomorphic fields with tower compatibility; the audit itself records both as "partial", and neither library proves them, so the layer states mathematics that is not built.

That layer owns nodes, the κ̄[[x,y]]/(xy) local normal form, normalisation with the conductor sequence, and the dual graph with p_a = Σ g_v + b₁(Γ) — the normalisation/node and dual-graph half of this substage.

Layers 1–2 of that roadmap own generator/parity-check matrices, encoding maps, dimension formulae and minimum distance, which is FF.4's stated acceptance criterion; FF.4 keeps only the evaluation/residue codes.

review.notes: All 133 cited declarations were re-looked-up in the pinned index and re-read in the Lean sources: every one exists at the cited library, file and line (only Mathlib's abbrev LinearMap.IsRefl.liftQ₂ is absent from the index, and it is present in the file), and none of the 141 cited files contains a sorry (the two grep hits are prose in docstrings). Statements, hypotheses and generality were checked against the targets; one citation was misread (LPV.4) and has been corrected. Every absent or partial claim was re-searched independently by concept across declarations.tsv and both source trees — q-de Rham/prisms/Λ-rings/animated rings/décalage/de Rham–Witt/truncation sets/syntomic/spectra; nearby and vanishing cycles, lisse and constructible sheaves, Verdier duality, perverse t-structures, blow-ups, Veronese, Bertini, dual varieties, tame and wild inertia, Abhyankar, quasi-unipotence, monodromy filtrations, p-adic Lie groups; Weil numbers, Rosati, Tate modules, Kuga–Sato, Eichler–Shimura, compatible systems; zeta functions of varieties and function fields, Euler products by closed-point degree, Fatou, Künneth, trace formulas, Hodge index and surface intersection theory, Pfaffians; Kloosterman, Artin–Schreier, Hasse–Davenport, Berlekamp/Cantor–Zassenhaus/Rabin, Galois rings, linearised and permutation polynomials, linear recurring sequences, Reed–Solomon/BCH/AG codes, finite upper half-planes. Two genuine misses were found (Tau Ceti's column orthogonality, Tau Ceti's unipotent API); everything else held. Verdicts are consistent with the target labels throughout; the remaining five "process" verdicts (HQ.7, R34.3, R34.4, WC.7, FF.5) were confirmed against the layer descriptions as import, acceptance-test or handoff layers that state no theorem of their own. All 66 duplicate layer ids exist in the atlas; the sampled overlap claims are accurate, and an atlas-wide keyword sweep of all 1962 layer descriptions found three further overlaps, now added.
